First, note:  
- Europe/Athens is EET (UTC+2) today, but in 1264, time zones didn’t exist; we must assume the question intends modern time zone rules applied to that historical date.  
- US/Eastern is UTC-5 (or UTC-4 during DST).  
- April 1 is before any DST in US/Eastern (DST starts second Sunday in March in modern rules, but 1264 predates DST; so likely standard time UTC-5).  
- Athens is UTC+2 (no DST in April in modern rules).  

Time difference: UTC+2 to UTC-5 = 7 hours behind Athens.  

1:00 Athens → subtract 7 hours → 18:00 previous day (March 31).  

FINAL_ANSWER: March 31, 18:00
